column1: TD - Backend - Implement Feedback Retrieval and Filtering
column32:
This task involves updating the backend feedback retrieval flow to support an additional date range filter parameter when querying paginated review data. The implementation should allow clients to request feedback within a specific start and end date while preserving the existing filters for category, article, and rating. The solution must follow SOLID principles, keep responsibilities clearly separated, validate and handle date range inputs safely, and avoid regressions in the current feedback retrieval features.

*Acceptance criteria*

* The feedback retrieval endpoint accepts optional start date and end date query parameters for filtering results by date range.
* When a valid date range is provided, the backend returns only feedback records created within the specified range while preserving existing category, article, rating, and pagination filters.
* Invalid date inputs, missing required range values, or a start date later than the end date are handled with clear validation errors and do not break existing behavior.
* The implementation keeps filtering logic separated from controllers and follows SOLID principles to maintain readability, testability, and extensibility.
* Existing feedback retrieval features continue to work as before when no date range filter is provided.

column32:
Message and idea: [https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1789664672586879|https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1789664672586879|smart-link] 

*On Boarding Flow Redesign*
Hey [@Aren Barge|https://cordobalegal.enterprise.slack.com/team/U08BPCRMQBU], hope you're doing well today!
Continuing from last Tuesday's meeting — kicking off a thread on the onboarding flow redesign, triggered by the duplicate-email issue we found in Forth. Below: the problem, how it works today, and three options to solve it, with pros and cons. Continue in this thread.

*On Boarding Flow Redesign*

*_Problem:_* The lack of duplicate-email verification in Forth means that, at login or onboarding time, CP has no way to reliably identify which account someone is trying to access.
*_Goal:_* Don't bring that problem into CP — the project hasn't launched yet, which is our chance to prevent it from the start and guarantee every user's email is unique in our own database.

*_How it works today (1.27.0):_*

# Login (email + password, password not validated)
# Silent redirect to onboarding if no account exists
# Confirm code — sent by email
# Create password
# Verify identity — SSN + date of birth
# Accept terms
# Done

Problems:

* The password serves no purpose and creates confusion/support calls
* An email search can resolve to the wrong account if two people share that email in Forth by mistake
* There's no duplicate detection at all.

!image (10).png|width=684,alt="image (10).png"!

*The three options*
+Before diving in: our recommendation is Option 3 below+ — it closes the same "wrong account" risk at a fraction of the cost. That said, we'd recommend reading all three, since Options 1 and 2 are what we discussed using the Account ID for last week.

*Options 1 and 2* both start from the same foundation: email is dropped as the identifier, and identity is verified with SSN + DOB as the first step, before any sensitive data is collected.

_Shared base flow_

# Login → "First time logging in?"
# Accept Terms & Privacy Policy
# Verify identity — SSN + DOB

3.1. Search Forth by SSN + DOB — 0 results: retry / 1 result: continue / 2+ results: contact us (rare case)
3.2. Check the email — already in our local system, or duplicated in Forth? +*_This is where the two options diverge._*+

# Confirm OTP — SMS, or email if there was a single result (user's choice)
# Create password
# Done

*_Option 1 — allow a secondary email_*
If there's a duplicate, the user is warned and given a choice: a secondary email just for the portal login, or contact us. Choosing a secondary email means entering it, confirming it, and confirming ownership with its own OTP (by email).
_Pros_

* The user can always get in, even with a duplicated email — fewer support calls.

_Cons_

* Reopens the work of decoupling the portal login from Forth's email.
* Most people take the fast path instead of reporting it, so Forth's data never actually gets cleaned up.
* Onboarding gets longer for anyone who sets up a secondary email — one more step, with its own OTP.

!image (11).png|width=684,alt="image (11).png"!

*_Option 2 — block and ask them to reach out_*
If there's a duplicate, there's no alternative — straight to contacting us.
_Pros_

* Forces every real duplicate to get resolved at the source — helps clean up Forth's data over time.
* Simpler to build and maintain.

_Cons_

* Anyone affected by a real duplicate is fully blocked until support resolves it — guaranteed support call.

!image (12).png|width=684,alt="image (12).png"!

*Option 3 — Keep email, fix the backend verification only*

# Login → "First time logging in?"
# Accept Terms & Privacy Policy
# Enter your email

3.1. Search Forth by that email — counts non-co-app matches instead of taking the first one

* 1 match → continues to 3.2
* 2+ matches → Contact us, account creation blocked

3.2. Check for duplicate email in our own DB

* duplicate → Contact us, account creation blocked
* clean → continues

# Confirm OTP — email (unchanged, {{ObStart}})
# Create password (unchanged, {{ObNewPassword}})
# Verify identity — SSN + DOB (unchanged, {{ObVerify}} — stays as a backstop)
# Done ({{ObCompleted}})


*Pros*

* Surgical fix — counting matches instead of taking the first one closes the "wrong account" risk, without touching anything else.
* Much cheaper — barely adds new steps, today's onboarding stays almost untouched.
* No need to touch Snowflake — email search already works through Forth's existing API; SSN + DOB would likely require it.
* Still surfaces real Forth duplicates for support to fix, same as Option 2.
* {{ObVerify}} is already a backstop if a wrong match ever slips through.

*Cons*

* A real duplicate fully blocks the user — guaranteed support call.

!image (13).png|width=684,alt="image (13).png"!



*_Decisions already made_*

* Terms & Privacy move to the front in all three options — today sensitive data is collected before the user agrees to how it's used.
* Identity verification (SSN + DOB) also moves to the front in Options 1 and 2; in Option 3 it stays exactly where it is today, as a backstop.
* For Options 1 and 2, dropped the "What's my Customer ID" lookup screen — exposing an unauthenticated SSN+DOB search is an unnecessary risk, and it's no longer needed since that's now the first step of the flow itself.
* For options 1 and 2, Email isn't used to identify anyone during onboarding because Forth's email data isn't reliable.
* How we'd resolve an already-flagged duplicate: ask the other person to update their email from their Profile (already live today); if that's too slow in practice, build an internal tool to force it later.

*The question*
In short: what do we prioritize — cost and simplicity (Option 3), fewer support calls (Option 1), or the strongest possible data-quality signal on Forth's duplicates (Option 2)?

column32:
*Description*

In the dashboard's Creditors and Learning Center cards, the "View All" button only navigates when the text itself is clicked — clicking the chevron icon next to it does nothing, even though it's visually part of the same button.

Both cards use the same pattern: a {{Button}} with an {{endIcon}}, wrapping a separate {{Link}} around only the text. This is confirmed in {{Creditors.tsx}} and {{LearningCenter.tsx}}, the only two places in the codebase with this pattern. column1: CP - WEB - Dashboard Creditors card shows settlement percentage based on payment count instead of amount
column32:
*Description*

The Creditors card on the dashboard shows a percentage next to each creditor ({{payMadePercentage}}), calculated as the number of payments made divided by the total number of payments. This doesn't reflect actual progress, since it ignores the dollar amount of each payment — a creditor could show a low percentage while most of the settlement amount has already been paid, or vice versa.

This was reviewed with Daniel Pardo and approved by Guillermo Malagón: the dashboard card should instead use the amount-based percentage (paid amount relative to the total settlement amount), consistent with how progress is already calculated in the Creditors section's own creditor list.

!image-20260914-212137.png|width=684,alt="image-20260914-212137.png"!

*Initial Findings*

* The correct amount-based field ({{settledCompletedPercentage}}) already exists in the {{contactDebts}} query and is already used by the Creditors section's list — this fix only requires switching which field the dashboard card reads, no backend or query changes needed.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -The percentage shown next to each creditor in the dashboard Creditors card reflects the amount paid relative to the total settlement amount, not the count of payments made.-
* -The value matches what's shown for the same creditor in the Creditors section's own list.-

column1: Web - Improve OTP screen UX (focus, validation, error feedback, sizing)
column32:
*Description*

{{OtpForm}} (shared across login, onboarding, and profile modals) has several UX rough edges found during review. This ticket groups the contained fixes.

*Initial Findings*

* Accepts non-digit characters and spaces ({{validateChar}} only checks non-empty).
* No auto-focus on the first box.
* No auto-submit on completing the 6th digit.
* Box width isn't capped, so boxes render wider on tablet-size screens than on desktop.
* "Resend code" button has no loading indicator.
* Failed attempts show no error state on the boxes — toast only, code stays untouched.
* {{aria-label}} hardcoded in English.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* First box auto-focuses on screen load.
* Completing 6 digits auto-submits on the first attempt only; a failed attempt requires manual "Submit" afterward.
* Boxes accept numeric input only (typed and pasted).
* Failed attempt shows a visual error state on the boxes without clearing them; clears on next edit.
* "Resend code" shows a loading indicator while in progress.
* Box width stays consistent across screen sizes.
* Error notification visually distinguishes "wrong" vs "expired" code.
* {{aria-label}} is localized.

*Out of scope:* {{CreateNewPassword}}'s plain OTP input, orphaned {{ChangePasswordOtp}}, resend-countdown clock-skew, digit-shift-on-delete (library limitation).

01/Sep/26 10:24 AM;712020:fd36cadf-9806-42d0-93a9-02002d8431e5;[~accountid:712020:313307ce-3202-4da7-b5a3-adcbee32f188] 

Moving this to Blocked.

While investigating this ticket I traced the call flow end-to-end: {{KazooController::handle()}} ({{app/Http/Controllers/Kazoo/KazooController.php}}) is invoked by Kazoo via {{POST /kazoo/number/handle}}, and it decides {{is_caller_known}} based on {{block_collectors}} and the creditor/blocked-phone tables. On the Kazoo side, the callflow this app provisions per account ({{KazooAPIClient::createCallFlow}}, see the {{is_lawyer_required}} module in {{app/Integrations/KazooAPIClient.php}}) matches a live custom Erlang module I found on the telephony server ({{cf_is_lawyer_required.beam}} on {{logic1}}). I decompiled it and confirmed it only reads a custom channel variable ({{Is-Creditor}}) to decide the branch — it does not call our backend directly.

I need to find where that {{Is-Creditor}} variable actually gets set (i.e., whatever component makes the real HTTP call to {{/kazoo/number/handle}}), since that's outside this repo. I've ruled out FreeSWITCH ({{fs1}}) as the source — no custom Lua/{{mod_xml_curl}}/dialplan curl logic is loaded there, only stock {{mod_kazoo}} — and there's no matching source tree on {{logic1}} either (the {{compile_info}} in the beam file points to {{/usr/local/src/applications/callflow/src/module/cf_is_lawyer_required.erl}}, which doesn't exist on that server).

Based on the CBMA Confluence documentation, the custom Kazoo/Erlang code lives in a separate repository ({{gitlab.velvetech.com/forth-new/cordoba/kazoo}}) that I don't currently have access to. I need access to that repo to locate the actual source for {{cf_is_lawyer_required}} and whatever module sets {{Is-Creditor}}, so I can confirm the real end-to-end flow and safely make changes here without breaking the Kazoo-side integration.

Could someone grant me access, or point me to who owns/maintains that repo?

thanks

column1: CX - Spike - Investigate Kazoo Webhook for Voicemail Availability
column32:
*Background*: Currently, our users don’t have the ability to filter out corrupted voicemails from the app, since we fetch these values from the Kazoo API directly in the client code.



*Goal*: Determine if Kazoo provides a webhook when a new voicemail is saved in our Kazoo DB (CouchDB). 

*This spike intends to answer the following questions*:

* Whether Kazoo provides a webhook/event for voicemail creation or availability.
* What events are available and when they are triggered.
* What information is included in the webhook payload.
* Whether the event can reliably indicate that the voicemail audio is available and valid.
* Whether Kazoo provides any mechanism to detect failed/corrupted voicemail files.
* How CreditorX could consume and process the webhook? Would this require backend changes?
* What happens if the webhook is not delivered.
* Whether additional validation against Kazoo would still be required.
* Any security/authentication requirements for consuming the webhook.
* Risks, limitations, and suggestions



*Resources*: [https://docs.2600hz.com/developers/rest/webhooks/webhooks/|https://docs.2600hz.com/developers/rest/webhooks/webhooks/|smart-link]

column1: CX - Spike - Investigate CreditorX Endpoint for Voicemail Validation
column32:
*Background*: Currently, our users don’t have the ability to filter out corrupted voicemails from the app, since we fetch these values from the Kazoo API directly in the client code.

*Goal*: Investigate the feasibility of creating an endpoint for the [CX-backend |https://github.com/cordoba-tech/creditorx-backend]that determines whether a voicemail is valid (playable) and available for a user to play.


*This spike intends to answer the following questions*:

* What information is currently available from Kazoo to determine whether a voicemail is valid or corrupted?
* Whether the CX-backend can reliably validate a voicemail before returning it to the mobile applications. (look for alternatives such as [ffmpeg|https://ffmpeg.org/])
* What the endpoint contract should look like? (endpoint design proposal)
* Whether validation should happen:
** When retrieving the voicemail list.
** When requesting/downloading an individual voicemail.
** Or through another mechanism.
* What should happen when Kazoo returns an invalid, corrupted, or unavailable voicemail? _For now, the team has decided to keep them as it is_.
* The expected performance and scalability impact of performing this validation through the backend? (Consider the spike in memory usage used to perform the validation of the audio)
* Whether any caching mechanism would be beneficial.
* What changes would be required on iOS and Android to consume the endpoint?
* Risk, limitation and suggestions
